name: Carina
introduction: is the Keel of the great ship Argo Navis, which carried Jason and the Argonauts. The ancient ship was so large that Nicolas-Louis de Lacaille divided it into three constellations in the 1750s: Carina, Puppis and Vela. Carina lies in the southern Milky Way and is best seen from the Southern Hemisphere.

sections.title: What makes it special
paragraphs: [Canopus](hip:30438) is the second-brightest star in the night sky, after Sirius. It is a white giant about 310 light-years away, thousands of times more luminous than the Sun. Because it is so bright and far from the Sun’s direction, spacecraft have long used it as a guide star for navigation.

Carina also contains one of the most extraordinary stars known: Eta Carinae, a pair of massive stars more than a hundred times the mass of the Sun. In the 1840s, it erupted and briefly became the second-brightest star in the sky, blasting out the twin lobes of the Homunculus Nebula.

sections.title: Notable stars
paragraphs: [Miaplacidus](hip:45238) is a white giant 113 light-years away. [Avior](hip:41037) and [Aspidiske](hip:45556), together with two stars of Vela, form the False Cross, which is sometimes mistaken for the Southern Cross.
[Theta Carinae](hip:52419) is the brightest member of IC 2602, a young cluster known as the Southern Pleiades.

sections.title: Beyond the stars
paragraphs: The Carina Nebula, about 7,500 light-years away, is several times larger than the Orion Nebula and one of the brightest star-forming regions in the sky. Its pillars and cliffs, including the “Cosmic Cliffs” captured by the James Webb Space Telescope in 2022, are sculpted by the radiation of massive young stars. The rich open cluster NGC 3532 lies nearby.
